column1: # One verdict per published API method. `gates api-coverage` holds this,
# testdata/api-surface.json and the code to each other, and runs in
# `used` names the client method that implements it. `out` says why this
# server does not call it. Every one of the 38 methods Calendar v3
# publishes has a row: a published method with no verdict fails the
# gate, a client call with no row fails, and a verdict for a method that

column4: reason
gapi.DeleteACL, behind unshare_calendar; it publishes no sendNotifications and Google sends none on a removal
acl.list returns every rule in one request; a single-rule read has no caller
gapi.InsertACL, behind share_calendar for a new rule; sendNotifications is always sent, because Google defaults it to true, unlike sendUpdates on an event
gapi.ListACL, behind list_sharing and get_calendar's exposure
gapi.PatchACL, behind share_calendar for a role change; a change to a rule is always a patch
PUT: replaces the rule whole; a change is always a patch (D-27)
needs a public HTTPS webhook; a stdio server has nowhere to put one (D-82)
gapi.DeleteCalendarListEntry, behind manage_calendar unsubscribe: the list entry goes, the calendar stays
gapi.GetCalendarListEntry, behind get_calendar and calendar resolution
gapi.InsertCalendarListEntry, behind manage_calendar subscribe
gapi.ListCalendars, behind list_calendars
gapi.PatchCalendarListEntry, behind manage_calendar for the per-user overrides: color, hidden, selected, the name this user gave it, notifications
PUT: replaces the entry whole; a change is always a patch (D-27)
needs a public HTTPS webhook, which a stdio server cannot offer (D-82)
gapi.ClearCalendar, behind clear_calendar: gated by GCAL_ENABLE_DESTRUCTIVE and confirm, and refused on anything but the primary calendar, which is what Google documents it for
gapi.DeleteCalendar, behind delete_calendar: gated by GCAL_ENABLE_DESTRUCTIVE and confirm, and refused on the primary, which Google does not delete
gapi.GetCalendar, behind get_calendar for a calendar not in the list
gapi.InsertCalendar, behind create_calendar; never retried, because Google mints the id and a blind retry makes a second calendar
gapi.PatchCalendar, behind manage_calendar for the calendar itself: title, description, location and time zone, which everybody subscribed to it sees
requires a Workspace admin privilege and useAdminAccess=true; this server authenticates as one ordinary user and never requests admin access (D-82)
PUT: replaces the calendar whole; a change is always a patch (D-27)
stops a push channel; there are none, because every watch method is out (D-82)
gapi.GetColors, behind get_settings
gapi.DeleteEvent, behind cancel_event for a whole event; one occurrence is a status: cancelled patch instead
gapi.GetEvent, behind get_event
carries a private copy of an event between systems, preserving iCalUID and organizer: a migration tool, not a scheduling one, with different failure modes (D-82)
gapi.InsertEvent, behind create_event and the second half of a this_and_following update, with a client-generated id; never retried, because Google does not promise to catch a repeated id
gapi.ListInstances, behind list_instances
gapi.ListEvents, behind list_events, search_events and list_changes
gapi.MoveEvent, behind move_event
gapi.PatchEvent, behind update_event, cancel_event on one occurrence, and respond_to_event; a change to an event is always a patch
parses a natural-language string, but gives no control over the time zone and does not report which fields it set; the model calling this server is a better parser (D-84)
PUT: drops attendees, RSVPs and recurrence when they are omitted, which is why a change is always a patch (D-27)
needs a public HTTPS webhook, which a stdio server cannot offer (D-82)
gapi.QueryFreeBusy, behind check_availability; batched at 50, the most calendars one query takes
settings.list returns every setting in one request
gapi.ListSettings, behind get_settings and the account's zone, the last place a time zone is looked for
needs a public HTTPS webhook, which a stdio server cannot offer (D-82)
